atoms.b: Coordinating conjunctions are linking words. They join together words or ((++phrases paragraphs)) that are equally important to the sentence.

instruction.text: Are these independent clauses or is it a compound sentence?

atoms.a: It is cold outside. The sun is shining.

end.text: The sentences “It is cold outside.” and “The sun is shining.” are both independent clauses. They can be joined with a comma and a coordinating conjunction.

atoms.a: It is cold outside, but the sun is shining.

end.text: This newly formed sentence is called a compound sentence.

atoms.b: The most common coordinating conjunctions are for, ((++and are)), nor, but, or, yet and so.
atoms.sound: ssml: The most common coordinating conjunctions are. <break time='500ms'/> for.<break time='500ms'/> and. <break time='500ms'/> nor.<break time='500ms'/> but. <break time='500ms'/> or. <break time='500ms'/> yet.<break time='500ms'/> and so.

end.text:
You can remember these conjunctions by using the acronym FANBOYS:
For
And
Nor
But
Or
Yet
So

instruction.text: Is this a compound sentence? Select the correct button.

hint.text: Remember: a compound sentence combines two independent clauses with a comma and a coordinating conjunction.

atoms.a: We could go to an art exhibition, or we could watch a film at home.
When my brother was younger, he believed in the tooth fairy.
His sister gave him flowers, for it was his birthday.
She watered the plants before leaving for the airport.
Paula mowed the lawn, and I trimmed the hedges.
He realised that it was time to make amends.
